Trickle v12 — Decision Board

One board for the whole v12 cycle. Each phase adds a section with test graphics and the questions Tarun answers; answers go to claude/v12_decisions.md. Constraint throughout: UPI linkage or manual entry, no SMS.

Phase 1 Recovery audit

Decided (Tarun, 1 Oct)

  • 5 tabs: Home · Income · Spending · Savings · Insights. The All spends list (with spend detail) lives in Spending.
  • Home bell: an activity log of every action (income split, sweeps, subscriptions paid, moves, splits). The few items that need action sit at the top. Soft dot, no count badge.
  • Tab intros: every tab has a one-page intro, shown on the first visit and reopened from a small "?".
  • Next money in card on Home by default, with no ₹.
  • What changed: one card in Insights; month by month is one tap deeper.
  • Deep views (Sankey, spend range, time of day) go in the Insights library, not on the default board.
  • Full editing (jars, budgets, period, savings share, subscriptions, UPI IDs) lives in each tab's settings, one decision per screen.
  • The rest of the MUST / NICE / NO list is accepted as recommended, with depth, and remapped onto the 5 tabs.

v11 is clear but thin. Every feature, flow, insight, chart and setting from v2 to v11, with what v11 kept, what it dropped, and what should come back without putting numbers or budgets on Home.

Questions for Tarun

Answered on 1 Oct. The decisions at the top of this section replace these options.

Q1

Where does the All spends list live?

  • A · Money › "All spends" row (list + filters + spend detail)
  • B · Inside each jar only
  • C · Search from Insights

Recommend A. Trust needs one plain list; Money already holds the numbers, Home stays clean.

Q2

Can Home gain one calm fact card: "Next money in · Allowance in 9 days"?

  • A · Yes, default Home card (no ₹ until tap)
  • B · Library only
  • C · No

Recommend A. A date, not a budget; it reduces anxiety near month end without breaking the no-budget rule.

Q3

How do comparison insights return (this vs last month by jar, month by month, top places)?

  • A · One "What changed" card on Insights: words + tile rows, month-by-month one tap deeper
  • B · Three separate library cards
  • C · Keep them out

Recommend A. One card, one question; depth carries the long view.

Q4

How much editing comes back?

  • A · Edit jars (add/rename/amount), weekly or payday period, savings share, income sources — all in Money/Settings
  • B · Only jar amounts
  • C · None; setup again to change

Recommend A. Real students differ from the 5 starter jars; editing lives one layer down so Home is untouched.

Q5

Do the v9 deep views (Sankey flow, spend range, time of day) return?

  • A · Yes, in an Insights library, not on the default board
  • B · Sankey only, as the month-story card
  • C · No

Recommend A. They were liked as discovery views; library keeps the default board at 3–4 cards.

Q6

Should one "for you" card return (sort an unknown payment, settle a split, renewal tomorrow)?

  • A · Yes, max one at a time on Home, no badge or count
  • B · Only as notifications
  • C · No

Recommend A. Unsorted payments silently break every insight; one card keeps the one-decision rule.

Recommendation

Primary · G5

Merging rows

₹100 tiles in rows of 10 with a gap after 5, exactly as learned in v11. When a row is complete it fuses into one pill (₹1,000) with a notch at ₹500. When you pay, the pill cracks back into tiles and some of them leave. Up to 90% less visual noise, and the unit never changes.

Alternative · G8 / G1

Liquid-fill tiles + glow for position

If G5 tests badly, use G8 (the same grid with a friendlier partial tile). The dot-matrix glow (G1) is kept for position views either way: calendar, time of day and the Home pace glow.

Large-amount collapse

  • Below ₹1,000: loose tiles
  • ₹1,000–₹10,000: whole rows as pills plus loose tiles
  • Above ₹10,000: ten rows become one ₹10,000 square (a 2×2 notch), then pills, then tiles
  • Collapse is still made of tiles; tap to expand

Key style

  • "■ = ₹100" once per screen, on the first tile visual
  • Repeated in each tab's "?" intro, with "a full row = ₹1,000"
  • Size follows the surface: airy (Home, pay) · regular (tabs) · compact (Insights)

Questions for Tarun

The recommended option is highlighted. Reply with letters, for example "P2-Q1 A".

P2-Q1

Which tile form should v12 use?

  • A · Merging rows (G5): ₹100 tiles, and a complete ₹1,000 row fuses into one pill
  • B · Dot-matrix glow (G1) everywhere
  • C · Keep the v11 grid (F) as it is

Recommend A. It keeps the learned ₹100 unit and counting but cuts visual noise, and rows splitting back into tiles gives motion a job.

P2-Q2

How do large amounts collapse?

  • A · Full ₹1,000 rows merge into pills; above ₹10,000, 10 rows become one ₹10,000 square
  • B · No merging; above 100 tiles show the number only
  • C · Switch to a proportion strip (G6) above ₹1,000

Recommend A. The same tile unit at every scale, with no second glyph: a pill is a row and a square is ten rows, both visibly made of tiles.

P2-Q3

Where does the dot-matrix glow belong?

  • A · Only on position views (calendar, time of day, Home pace), never as money
  • B · As the money tile in the B&W/dark look
  • C · Nowhere

Recommend A. It is beautiful on dark, but its partials are vague. Keeping it for dates and pace also keeps "position views look different from tiles" (a v11 rule).

P2-Q4

Which density levels should ship?

  • A · Size follows the surface: airy on Home and the pay moment, regular in tabs, compact in Insights
  • B · A user setting (compact / regular / airy)
  • C · One size everywhere

Recommend A. Home holds 30 tiles or fewer and Insights needs 100 or more. The surface decides the size, which saves the user a setting.

P2-Q5

Key style?

  • A · "■ = ₹100" once per screen on the first tile visual, plus a line in each tab's "?" intro
  • B · A tiny persistent key in every card corner
  • C · Taught in onboarding only

Recommend A. It worked in v11. The new tab intros are a natural second place for it, so cards stay clean.

Top 3

R4 · 4.75

Cup tile

  • + "A square is ₹100; it fills like a cup." One sentence.
  • + Remainder reads as a level (½ full = ₹50), even at 6px.
  • + Pay drains the cup, income fills it; bars crack into cups.
  • − ₹10 is only a thin floor line.
  • − ₹6,350 = 10 marks, ₹1,23,000 = 18: fine on Home, dense in lists.
R1 · 4.35

Crumb · Tile · Pill · Block

  • + The one Tarun likes; pure base-10, area-honest.
  • + The crumb dot is visibly "not a tile".
  • − An area-true ₹10 dot is about 1px; ₹25 and ₹50 are hard to tell apart.
  • − A dot growing into a square is a weaker animation than a cup filling.
R2 · 4.40

Snapping crumbs

  • + Change is countable: ₹25 quarters, four make a tile.
  • + Best accumulate story: 4 chais visibly snap into ₹100.
  • − ₹10 and ₹99 get odd partial quarters.
  • − A second sub-unit (₹25) to learn.

Recommendation (hybrid): use R4 cup tiles on the R1 crumb → tile → pill → block ladder as the single static rule. Add R2's snap as motion: when cups add up to ₹100 they merge into a solid tile, and when 10 tiles fill a row they fuse into a pill. Add R3's tap to zoom (scored 4.25, 4th) as an interaction layer, not a static form, as the way to get exact amounts (block → tiles → ₹10s). This keeps one rule everywhere and needs no numbers on cards. Rejected: R10 log (dishonest), R12 cash (246 marks), R14 abacus and R9 icons (marks not sized to value).

  • B · Shows the exact ₹ in a tooltip

P2b-Q4

Should Savings and Income round to whole tiles while Spending stays exact (R11)?

  • A · No: one rule everywhere
  • B · Yes: savings/income round, spending exact

Recommend A. Two rules cost learnability; at ≥₹1,000 the cup remainder is already small next to the bars.

Phase 2c Money visualization research

How to show money so a student understands it at a glance and is not scared to open the app. 39 sources (33 verified, 6 marked unverified), 20 methods drawn with the locked tile ladder on one sample: ₹350 meal, ₹6,000 budget with ₹2,100 left, four ₹25 chais, ₹9,000 income, ₹8,000 goal at 52%, and a week that ran ₹600 over the last.

Three rules the research agrees on

  • Show the whole, always. Spent tiles stay as outlines, so ₹2,100 is read against ₹6,000 (icon arrays fix denominator neglect).
  • Lead with what is left, never with red. People stop opening accounts that show bad news (ostrich effect); calm framing keeps them looking.
  • Translate into their own units. One short perspective line with a familiar thing (their chai, a third of the month) improves recall and estimation.

Where the top 8 go

HomeM1 leftover-first tiles + M15 ratio line + M3 per-day under it
Pay momentM2 ghost tiles before confirm, tiles lift out after
SpendingM4 crumbs stacking + M5 equivalents in spend detail
SavingsM6 to-go outlines + M13 ETA path
IncomeM7 part-to-whole pills
InsightsM8 ghost comparison in "What changed"; M11/M12/M9 in library

Sources

Each card: the finding, then what it means for Trickle. Dashed = could not open the source; treat as unverified.

Haroz et al. 2015

Pictographs that ARE the data cause no performance cost and can help memory and engagement; decorative extra images distract.

Trickle: The ₹100 tile is itself the datum, so it earns the Isotype benefit; keep illustrations out of tile areas.

Park et al. 2018

One mark per unit "minimizes the need for the user to consider data abstraction" and matches how novices build with physical tokens.

Trickle: Tiles can regroup across Home/Spending/Income (split by jar, by day) and still be the same tiles.

Neurath/Kinross 1995

Isotype rule: "in representing quantities, repeat a unit, don't enlarge it"; also "don't say more than you know".

Trickle: Confirms the ladder: pills and blocks are merged repeats of tiles, never a bigger tile.

Cleveland & McGill 1984

Accuracy ranking: position on common scale > nonaligned position > length/direction/angle > area > volume/curvature > shading/saturation.

Trickle: Align pills to a common left edge so comparisons are length on a common scale; never encode amount by colour depth.

Kosara 2019

Most area-based part-to-whole variants did worse than a pie; centred shapes hurt area judgement.

Trickle: Cup fill reads as a level from a shared floor (not a centred shrinking square) — keep it bottom-anchored.

Redmond 2019

Bars with decile markers / scale beat plain bars for part-to-whole; pies have natural anchors at quarters.

Trickle: A pill is literally ten deciles; the gap after 5 tiles gives a halfway anchor.

Garcia-Retamero et al. 2010

People over-attend numerators; icon arrays showing the whole fix denominator neglect, for young and old.

Trickle: Show spent tiles as outlines so ₹2,100 is always seen against ₹6,000.

Garcia-Retamero & Cokely 2013

Well-designed visual aids are "highly effective, transparent, and ethically desirable", most for low-numeracy people.

Trickle: Tiles help the students who most avoid numbers; never hide them behind a toggle.

Galesic et al. 2009 UNVERIFIED

(Abstract not opened — pages returned 403/429.) Widely cited for icon arrays improving accuracy for low-numeracy people.

Trickle: Supports M11; cite only alongside the verified 2010 paper.

Gigerenzer & Hoffrage 1995

Natural frequencies roughly tripled correct reasoning (46–50% vs 16–28%) over probabilities.

Trickle: Insights copy uses counts of days/tiles, never percentages.

Kay et al. 2016

Quantile dotplots (~20 countable dots) beat density plots for lay mobile users; 100+ dots lose the benefit.

Trickle: Home cards stay under ~25 marks — pills keep ₹2,100 at 3 marks; a "usual week" range can be 20 dots.

Barrio et al. 2016

Perspective sentences (ratios, ranks, unit changes) improved recall, estimation and error detection (n>3,200).

Trickle: "₹2,100 — about a third of your month" under the Home tiles.

Riederer et al. 2018

Familiar references beat precise obscure ones; multipliers 1–10 (esp. 1, ½) work best; benefit lasts six weeks.

Trickle: Pick equivalents from the student's own frequent spends (their chai, their mess meal); prefer "2 dinners" over "0.17 of rent".

Peters et al. 2006

Less numerate people are more swayed by framing and irrelevant affect.

Trickle: Neutral, consistent frames (left / to go) protect low-numeracy students from alarm.

Soman 2001

Past payments curb later spending only when the amount is rehearsed and the wealth depletes immediately.

Trickle: Pay moment (M2): tiles lift out of the balance the instant UPI confirms — rehearsal without a number to type.

Knutson et al. 2007

Excessive prices activated insula; price-period activity predicted purchase beyond self-report.

Trickle: Show the tiles a spend will take before confirming (ghost tiles), not after.

Prelec & Loewenstein 1998 UNVERIFIED

Pain of paying acts as self-regulation; less visible depletion (cards) dulls it.

Trickle: Tiles leaving = a soft pain-of-paying cue without red.

Heath & Soll 1996

People set category budgets; budgets constrain category-typical purchases (sometimes under-consumption).

Trickle: Jars as tile rows (M14); per-jar "left" is the main figure.

Antonides et al. 2011

Mental budgeters show better oversight of spending and accounts.

Trickle: Supports jars and per-day allowance.

Thaler 1999 UNVERIFIED

(Metadata verified; abstract not available on the page opened.) Foundational account of mental accounts.

Trickle: Background for jars.

Olafsson & Pagel 2018

People log in far less when balances are negative; logins jump when the balance turns positive.

Trickle: Lead with what is left, not what is gone; no alarm colours on Home.

Karlsson et al. 2009 UNVERIFIED

(Not opened; search listing only.) Investors look up portfolios less in down markets.

Trickle: Corroborates Olafsson & Pagel.

Tversky & Kahneman 1981

Same facts framed differently produce predictable preference shifts.

Trickle: "₹2,100 left", "₹3,840 to go" — never "you lost ₹3,900".

Kivetz et al. 2006

Effort rises as the goal nears; illusory progress (bonus stamps) speeds completion.

Trickle: Savings goal: outlined to-go tiles disappear; round-ups make first tiles fill fast.

Hershfield et al. 2011

Seeing an aged future self increased preference for later rewards.

Trickle: Light version: the goal ETA dot on a month path ("you, in February, with ₹8,000").

DeVoe & Pfeffer 2007 UNVERIFIED

(Metadata verified; no abstract on page.) Hourly pay makes people value time in money.

Trickle: Students rarely earn hourly; translate to "days of food money" instead of hours of work.

Whillans et al. 2017

Spending on time-saving purchases raised happiness more than material ones (n=6,271).

Trickle: Support for days-based framing (M10) in the library, not Home.

Li et al. 2010

Preparation → collection → integration → reflection → action; barriers cascade.

Trickle: Every money view should end in a possible action (move tiles, lower a jar).

Weiser & Brown 1995

"Calm technology engages both the center and the periphery of our attention, and moves back and forth."

Trickle: Home = periphery (tiles + one word); tap-to-zoom = centre.

Pousman et al. 2007 UNVERIFIED

(Not opened — 403.) Defines casual infovis for non-experts in everyday contexts.

Trickle: Background for ambient Home.

Lan et al. 2023

Review of 109 papers and 61 projects; emotion is a legitimate design target but the field lacks clear definitions.

Trickle: Pick a single affect per surface: Home calm, Pay neutral, Savings warm.

Kennedy & Hill 2018

Emotions are "vital components of making sense of data" in everyday use.

Trickle: Red, shaking or alarm motion carries meaning beyond the amount; avoid.

Boy et al. 2017

Anthropomorphic icons had no more effect on empathy than standard charts.

Trickle: No cute coin characters inside tiles; save personality for copy and motion.

YNAB 2016

Age of Money = days a rupee sits before use; higher means "your stress level will drop".

Trickle: Runway days (M9) as an Insights card.

Monzo 2023

Users missed "left to spend" and the "set to have £ left over" projection after its removal.

Trickle: Leftover-first Home is validated by real use.

Korostoff (n.d.)

Fixed unit ("10 px = $5M") plus relatable comparisons makes huge sums graspable.

Trickle: Same ₹100 tile everywhere + equivalents.

Dear Data 2015

Hand-drawn weekly personal data as "personal documentary"; slow, humane data.

Trickle: Weekly reflection card tone; tiles as a personal ledger, not a report.

Fi Money 2026

FIT rules automated saving from behaviour; consumer app shut 11 Mar 2026.

Trickle: Rule-triggered tile moves (e.g. round-ups) fit Savings.

Cleo (TME 2022)

Opt-in "roast mode" shames spending with humour; default is not roast.

Trickle: Avoid shame copy by default.

Questions for Tarun

P2c-Q1

What is the big number on Home?

  • A · ₹ left (₹2,100), tiles below
  • B · ₹ per day (₹175)
  • C · Runway days (6 days)

Recommend A. Left-to-spend is what people miss when gone (Monzo) and frames as remaining; per-day sits as the second line.

P2c-Q2

How do spent rupees look?

  • A · Outlined empty tiles
  • B · Faded solid tiles
  • C · Removed entirely

Recommend A. Outlines keep the whole visible (denominator neglect) without red; removal hides the budget, fading reads as "still mine".

P2c-Q3

Which equivalents unit?

  • A · From the student's own frequent spends (their chai, their meal)
  • B · Fixed staples (chai ₹25, thali ₹120)
  • C · No equivalents

Recommend A. Familiar references work best (Riederer 2018); fallback to B until two weeks of data exist.

P2c-Q4

"You spent more than last week" — how loud?

  • A · Ghost of last week + hatched extra + one perspective sentence
  • B · Amber status chip
  • C · Only if asked in Insights

Recommend A. Shows the gap as countable tiles, no alarm hue; amber invites ostrich avoidance.

P2c-Q5

Money-as-time framing?

  • A · Days of a jar ("1.2 days of food money")
  • B · Hours of work
  • C · None

Recommend A. Most students have no hourly wage; days-of-jar keeps the time lens without implying a job. Library only.

Phase 2d Tarun's sketches

Tarun drew one frame in Figma ("money Visualisation one"): the ₹100 dot and how dots fuse as amounts grow. Below: what it shows, his concept expanded to every kind of money moment, five new tiling ideas, a comparison and questions.

His sketch

KeyOne red dot labelled "Rs 100". The unit is a circle, not a square.
₹10,000 grid10 × 10 touching dots, no gaps. 67 red (rows 1–6 + seven of row 7), 33 green. Label "Rs 10000".
₹6,600Each row of 10 dots fuses into a capsule pill (₹1,000): 4 red pills, 2 green pills, then 6 loose green dots.
₹16,600One rounded-square block (₹10,000) on the left; the same pill column top-aligned on its right. Only 5 loose dots are visible (one is hidden in the layer), so it draws ₹16,500.
₹26,600Two blocks fused into one 2:1 rounded rectangle, same pill column.
₹46,600Four blocks fused into one big 2×2 rounded square, same pill column. Blocks are all red.

One frame only, so "the first one" is this whole system: dot → pill → block, laid out as blocks left, pills stacked right, loose dots under the pills. It matches the locked ladder exactly (₹100 / ₹1,000 / ₹10,000).

His scale steps, redrawn

Same five amounts in his layout, blocks kept apart by a hairline. Tap any one to zoom a level.

Tap an amount.

Expanded: Merging Dots, every money moment

Key: solid blue = left · outline = spent · green = saved · dashed blue = held for subscriptions · dashed green = owed to you · hatched = extra beyond plan · dotted grey = last week (ghost). No numbers would sit on Home; numbers here are for review.

X0

The ladder (Tarun's, kept)

A dot is ₹100. Ten dots fuse into a pill, ten pills into a block. Less than ₹100 fills a dot like a cup.

Repeat the unit, never enlarge it (Isotype); base-10 merge is area-true.

X1

Income arrives, then splits

₹9,000 came in. ₹6,000 went to this month, ₹499 is held for subscriptions, ₹2,501 went to savings.

Part-to-whole in the same unit (M7). Split happens at once on arrival so the budget is "real" from day one (mental accounting, Thaler; Heath & Soll).

X2

Budget by category

₹2,100 of ₹6,000 left. Food has the most left; Other is nearly done.

Whole always visible: spent stays as outlines (denominator neglect, Garcia-Retamero 2010). Counts, not %, read better (Gigerenzer & Hoffrage).

X3

Subscriptions: a reserved chunk

₹493 held for three subscriptions. Spotify is paid; the other two leave on their dates on their own.

Reserved dots are dashed: they are yours but already spoken for, so "left" never counts them (earmarking, Soman & Cheema 2011).

X4

One pay leaves: ₹350 meal

Tap Pay. Three and a half dots lift out and stay as outlines. ₹1,750 left.

Show the pay as tiles leaving, at the moment of pay (M2; pain of paying, Prelec & Loewenstein; Soman 2001).

X5

Four ₹25 chais fill one dot

Each chai fills a quarter. The fourth one completes a ₹100 dot.

Small repeats become visible as a whole tile (M4; "latte factor" made countable, frequency format).

X6

Big one-off: ₹2,400

₹2,400 left at once: two pills and four dots. That is about 7 of your usual dinners.

Large spends shown in the same unit, with one perspective line in their own buys (Barrio 2016; Riederer 2018). Marked once, no alarm.

X7

Empty jar and overspend

Fun is empty. The extra ₹250 came from Food, so Food now has ₹550 left.

No red (ostrich effect: people stop looking, Olafsson & Pagel 2018). Overspend is a move between jars, shown as hatched dots outside the jar.

X8

Split bill, money owed back

You paid ₹1,200. Your share is ₹300; ₹900 is coming back from three friends.

Owed money is drawn but dashed, so it is not counted as spendable until it arrives (honest "left").

X9

Refund

₹350 came back. Three and a half outlined dots refill and Food has ₹1,150 left again.

Reverse of the pay motion: outlines fill back in. Same rule, no new symbol.

X10

Savings goal at 52%

₹4,160 saved for the phone. ₹3,840 to go: about 4 more months at this pace.

Goal gradient: show "to go" shrinking (Kivetz 2006). Saved dots green, the rest outlined in the same shape.

X11

Month-end leftover → savings

₹400 was left on the 30th. It moved into savings.

A small win at month end; leftover becomes progress, not a reset (goal gradient, Kivetz).

X12

This week vs last week

You spent ₹600 more than last week, mostly on Friday food.

Ghost of last week + hatched extra + one sentence, no red (M8, locked).

X13

Where it went: categories compared

Food took the most: ₹2,200 of the ₹3,900 spent.

Aligned rows on a common baseline are read most accurately (Cleveland & McGill).

X14

Day view (the week)

Thursday was the big day. Wednesday you spent nothing.

Columns of 2 dots per day keep a week under ~25 marks; glow ring only marks today (position, locked).

New tiling concepts

Different from his and from Phase 2b's 14 systems. Each shows the same seven moments.

N1

Ticket strip

"A ticket is ₹100; ten make a strip (₹1,000). Paying tears tickets off; small buys shorten a ticket."

₹25 chai
₹350 meal
₹6,000 budget, ₹2,100 left
₹9,000 income split
₹499 subscription
Goal ₹8,000 at 52%
Four chais accumulate

Good: Tearing is a physical, felt metaphor for pain of paying; perforations keep counts visible inside a strip.

Risk: Strips read like a long bar; the ₹10,000 level (a booklet) needs its own shape.

N2

Day lanes

"What is left is pre-cut into days. Each day gets its share; today's share empties as you pay."

₹25 chai
₹350 meal
₹6,000 budget, ₹2,100 left
₹9,000 income split
₹499 subscription
Goal ₹8,000 at 52%

Not a daily amount: falls back to dots.

Four chais accumulate

Good: Turns "₹2,100 left" into "₹300 a day for a week" (per-day allowance, M3) without a number; best answer to "can I afford this today?".

Risk: Income, goals and subscriptions are not daily money; it needs a second form for them. Sliding shares daily can feel like a diet.

N3

Glass columns

"A glass holds ₹1,000 with ten marks (₹100 each). Money is liquid; spending lowers the level."

₹25 chai
₹350 meal
₹6,000 budget, ₹2,100 left
₹9,000 income split
₹499 subscription
Goal ₹8,000 at 52%
Four chais accumulate

Good: Continuous fill handles ₹25 and ₹350 with no crumb shape; drain/fill motion is natural; ~6–8 glasses for a month.

Risk: Level reading is less exact than counting (no discrete count, weaker than icon arrays); ₹10,000 = 10 glasses needs a jug.

N4

Bangles

"A bead is ₹100; ten beads close a bangle (₹1,000). Small buys fill a bead."

₹25 chai
₹350 meal
₹6,000 budget, ₹2,100 left
₹9,000 income split
₹499 subscription
Goal ₹8,000 at 52%
Four chais accumulate

Good: Keeps Tarun's round dots; a closed ring is a strong "complete" signal (goal gradient: you see the gap close).

Risk: Rings take more space than rows; 6+ bangles need two rows; ₹10,000 level (a stack of ten bangles) is hard to draw small.

N5

Hourglass

"Money left sits on top; every pay drops through and piles up below as outlines."

₹25 chai
₹350 meal
₹6,000 budget, ₹2,100 left
₹9,000 income split
₹499 subscription
Goal ₹8,000 at 52%
Four chais accumulate

Good: One picture holds left and spent with no subtraction; the drop is the pay animation; good Home hero.

Risk: Only one jar per glass; pile shape varies, so counts below are harder; goal reads oddly ("filling up" is reversed).

Comparison

Merging Dots (expanded)●●●●●●●●●●Low●●●●●FullHis form + every locked rule
N1 Ticket strip●●●●○●●●●○Med (tearing)●●●○○PartialNeeds a booklet for ₹10,000

Where the sketch differs from locked decisions

Red fillHe uses red + green fills. Locked/recommended: no red; spent = outlined, left = solid (P2c A1, P2c-Q2 rec. A). Kept his form, swapped red fill for outline.
Red/green pairThe most common colour-blind confusion; in B&W both read the same grey. Solid vs outline carries the meaning instead.
Fused blocks2 and 4 blocks fuse into one bigger shape. Area stays true, but seams vanish so you cannot count blocks, and a 2×2 square drifts towards "enlarge the icon" (A2). Expanded concept keeps a hairline gap between blocks.
Touching dotsNo gap between dots makes 30+ dots hard to count (marks rule ~20 on mobile). Expanded concept adds a 1px gap; pills still fuse.
Circle cupLocked crumb is a cup-filled tile. In a circle, fill height ≠ area (a half-height fill is exactly half; a quarter-height is ~20%). Small, but note it.
Label 16,600Frame shows ₹16,500 (hidden dot). Probably a sketch slip.

Questions for Tarun

P2d-Q1. What do red and green mean in your sketch?
  • A · red = spent, green = left
  • B · two categories / jars
  • C · just colour, no meaning

Recommendation: — — Decides whether it conflicts with outlined-spent.

P2d-Q2. Keep dots (circles) as the ₹100 unit instead of squares?
  • A · Circles everywhere (his)
  • B · Squares (Phase 2b)
  • C · Circles only on Home

Recommendation: A — Shape change does not break "1 unit = ₹100"; circles make pills look like fused dots, which teaches the ladder.

P2d-Q3. Should several ₹10,000 blocks fuse into one shape?
  • A · Keep separate blocks with a hairline gap
  • B · Fuse (his 2:1 and 2×2)
  • C · Fuse, tap to split

Recommendation: A — Countable blocks; fused 2×2 reads as one bigger thing.

P2d-Q4. Which new concept should be tested next to Merging Dots?
  • A · Day lanes (as a "today" view)
  • B · Hourglass (Home hero)
  • C · Ticket strip
  • D · None

Recommendation: A — Day lanes adds per-day allowance without a number; the others replace the ladder.

P2d-Q5. Spent dots: outline (rec.) or your red fill dimmed?
  • A · Outline
  • B · Dimmed fill
  • C · Your red

Recommendation: A — Outline keeps the whole visible with no alarm colour.

Phase 2e Dot system + concept deep-dive

Tarun's decisions after 2d: circles are the ₹100 unit with small gaps; spent = outlined, left = solid, no red; ladder crumb → dot → pill → block, blocks keep a hairline gap; the cup inside a circle must read by area. Below, his Merging Dots and five other concepts, each across the same 15 money moments.

Cup fill inside a circle, by area

  • A · Pie wedge (rec.) Area = share exactly. Quarters read as a clock: ₹25 = quarter past.
  • B · Concentric core A small disc grows from the centre; radius √share, so area is exact.
  • C · Area-true level Keeps the cup: liquid height solved so the AREA is the share. ₹25 sits at 0.30 height, not 0.25.
  • 2d · Height fill (old) For contrast: a quarter-height fill is only 20% of the area.

All concepts below use A, the pie wedge. Key for every state: solid blue = left · outline = spent · green = saved · dashed blue = held for subscriptions · dashed green = owed to you · hatched = extra beyond plan · dotted = last week · tinted wedge = small spends adding up.

Concepts × 15 states

A dot is ₹100. Ten dots in a row fuse into a pill (₹1,000); ten pills into a block (₹10,000). Blocks keep a hairline gap. Less than ₹100 fills a dot like a clock wedge.

Good: His own form; the purest isotype (repeat the unit, never enlarge it). Works for every kind of money.

Risk: Long rows for mid amounts (₹6,000–9,000 = 6–9 pills). Needs one more idea for "today".

A ticket is a ₹100 dot on a stub. Ten tickets make a perforated strip (₹1,000); ten strips bind into a booklet (₹10,000). Paying tears tickets off.

Good: Tearing is a felt metaphor for the pain of paying (Prelec & Loewenstein 1998); perforations keep the count visible.

Risk: Stock outlines add ink; strips read like a long bar. Tearing can feel like loss, raising anxiety slightly.

Comparison

ConceptLearnabilityResearch fit (2c)AnxietyScale ₹25→₹1,23,000Fits locked rulesBest tabNote
Merging Dots●●●●●●●●●●Low●●●●●Full (every locked rule)Home, Income, SavingsBase unit everywhere; his form.
Day lanes●●●●○●●●●●Med (diet feeling)●●○○○Full if used as a view of the same dotsSpendingPer-day allowance M3 without a number; P2c-Q1 puts per-day in Spending.
Glass columns●●●●●●●●●○Low●●●○○Partial (container ink; ladder kept)Spending (jars)Dots inside fix 2d's count problem; good jar metaphor.
Bangles●●●○○●●●○○Low●●○○○Partial (no common baseline)Savings (goal ring)Closing ring = goal gradient; poor for comparing.
Hourglass●●●●○●●●○○Med●●○○○Weak (one jar per picture; goals reversed)Home hero (optional)Left + spent in one picture; pay = drop.
Ticket strip●●●●○●●●●○Med (tearing)●●●○○Partial (stub ink; booklet is new shape)Spending (pay moment only)Tear is a strong pay-moment motion.

Concepts combine: they share the ₹100 dot, so one can be the unit and another a view of the same dots.

Recommendation

Use Merging Dots as the one base unit on every tab (Home, Income, Savings, Insights). Give Spending two views of the same dots: Day lanes for "this week / today" (per-day share stood upright) and Merging Dots rows for jars. Borrow two motions, not forms: the Hourglass drop for the pay animation and the Bangle close when a goal or a four-chai dot completes. Park Glass columns and Ticket strip.

Questions for Tarun

P2e-Q1. Which cup fill inside a dot?
  • A · Pie wedge (clock)
  • B · Concentric core
  • C · Area-true liquid level

Recommendation: A — Exact area, and ₹25 steps read as clock quarters, which teaches the four-chai moment.

P2e-Q2. Colour for "left": keep blue, or your green?
  • A · Blue left, green saved (now)
  • B · Green left, a second hue for saved
  • C · One ink colour; saved marked by a ring

Recommendation: A — Green is already "saved"; solid vs outline carries left vs spent, so hue is free for kind.

P2e-Q3. Adopt the combination?
  • A · Merging Dots base + Day lanes in Spending
  • B · Merging Dots everywhere only
  • C · Another mix

Recommendation: A — Day lanes answer "can I afford this today?" without a number on Home.

P2e-Q4. Which motions to borrow?
  • A · Hourglass drop (pay) + Bangle close (complete)
  • B · Ticket tear (pay)
  • C · Plain lift-out (2d)

Recommendation: A — Drop keeps the outline left behind; tearing reads as loss.

P2e-Q5. Day lanes overspend: borrow from tomorrow's lane?
  • A · Yes, tomorrow's lane shortens
  • B · No, show hatched extra only
  • C · Re-spread across all days

Recommendation: C — Re-spreading is gentler than a short tomorrow; less "diet" feeling.

Phase 3 Insight library

31 insights, each drawn 2–3 ways in the locked dot system with the same seed month (₹9,000 in, day 18 of 30; Food ₹2,500 · Travel ₹1,500 · Fun ₹2,000; Goa ₹4,160 of ₹8,000). The recommended form has the dark border.

Key (once): ● = ₹100, pill = ₹1,000, block = ₹10,000, wedge = under ₹100 · solid jar colour = left (Food amber, Travel blue, Fun plum) · outline = spent · green = savings only · dashed grey = held for subscriptions · dashed blue = owed to you · dotted = last period · hatched = extra beyond last period · glow = time or position only (no ₹).

Default set per tab

Home

Pace / day allowance · Jar left · Little things (Home) · Subscriptions held & next due · Next money in · Goal progress

Income

Income sources · Next money in · Income split · Where money sits

Spending

Pace / day allowance · Jar left · Repeat buys · Subscriptions held & next due · Owed to you

Savings

Goal progress · Goal ETA · Savings growth · Leftover rolled to savings

Insights

Small buys add up · Category share · What changed · Month story · Equivalents

Insights library (12): Category drift (month vs last) · Top places · Time of day · Weekday pattern · Calendar · Spend range · Big one-offs · Subscription yearly cost · Money flow (Sankey) · Savings rate · Money as time (days of a jar) · Month by month.

Insights × alternatives

Pace / day allowance

Can I afford this today?

SpendingglancedefaultHome-eligible

Why: Per-day allowance is the most actionable framing (M3: YNAB 2016; Gigerenzer & Hoffrage 1995 natural frequencies). Day lanes were adopted for Spending; overspend re-spreads, no blame. On Home it drops to the glow word only.

Jar left

How much is left per jar?

SpendingglancedefaultHome-eligible

Why: Leftover-first with the whole visible (M1, M14: Olafsson & Pagel 2018; Heath & Soll 1996 mental accounts). Rows share a left edge so jars compare on a common baseline (Cleveland & McGill 1984).

Little things (Home)

What small things add up?

HomeglancedefaultHome-eligible

Why: Home carries no numbers (P2c-Q1). Pie wedges stacking show crumbs adding up by area alone (M4: Haroz 2015; Soman 2001).

Repeat buys

Where do I keep going?

Spendingexploredefault

Why: Crumbs merging into ₹100 dots make the accumulation visible in the one unit (M4: Kay et al. 2016; Haroz 2015). The yearly view is the detail layer (rec #96).

Small buys add up

Do little buys matter?

Insightsexploredefault

Why: Same mechanism as repeat buys but across all places; the merge is the insight (Soman 2001 payment transparency).

Category share

Where does most of it go?

Insightsexploredefault

Why: A 100-dot waffle gives a frequency-format share ("46 of every 100", Gigerenzer & Hoffrage 1995; Garcia-Retamero 2010) and keeps the dot vocabulary; split pill loses countability.

What changed

What is different this week?

Insightsexploredefault

Why: One sentence + the ghost of last period with hatched extra (decided P2c-Q4; Lan et al. 2023 one-message charts). One change beats a list for low-load reading.

Category drift (month vs last)

Which jar changed?

Insightsdetaillibrary

Why: Ghost-of-last-period is the locked comparison language; dumbbell uses position (allowed) but adds a second vocabulary.

Top places

Who gets most of my money?

Spendingexplorelibrary

Why: Ranked rows on a shared baseline are the most accurate comparison (Cleveland & McGill 1984).

Time of day

When do I spend?

Insightsdetaillibrary

Why: Time is position, so glow is allowed (P2-Q3). A straight strip beats a ring for reading order (v6 radial clock was hard to read); the word "mostly late evenings" carries it.

Weekday pattern

Which days are heavy?

Insightsdetaillibrary

Why: Day lanes are already the Spending view, so the usual week reuses them (one vocabulary, Neurath).

Calendar

Which days were heavy?

Spendingexplorelibrary

Why: Calendar is position data: glow per day, today ringed. Dots-per-day is countable but dense at phone size.

Spend range

Steady or spiky?

Insightsdetaillibrary

Why: Kay et al. 2016: discrete outcome dots beat intervals for lay readers (M12); M11 frequency is the alt sentence.

Big one-offs

What was the big one?

Insightsexplorelibrary

Why: Perspective against the user's own usual buy (Barrio 2016; Riederer 2018).

Subscriptions held & next due

What leaves next?

SpendingglancedefaultHome-eligible

Why: Held money as dashed dots inside the budget, next due as glow on the month track (time = glow). Home shows only the track.

Subscription yearly cost

What does it cost a year?

Spendingdetaillibrary

Why: Annualising is the eye-opener behind cancelling (rec #81); pills keep the ladder.

Income sources

Where does my money come from?

Incomeexploredefault

Why: Part-to-whole pills (M7: Neurath; Park 2018). Income uses neutral ink shades, not green.

Next money in

When does money come next?

IncomeglancedefaultHome-eligible

Why: Time = position + glow; no ₹, so Home-eligible (decided Q2).

Income split

Where did new money go?

Incomeglancedefault

Why: M7 part-to-whole; the hourglass drop is the pay motion, not the static view.

Money flow (Sankey)

Where did all money go?

Insightsdetaillibrary

Why: v9's most-liked deep view; ribbon widths are on the same ₹ scale, nodes in category colour, spent ribbons outlined.

Savings rate

What share did I keep?

Savingsexplorelibrary

Why: Ratio as "2 of 10" is a natural frequency (Gigerenzer & Hoffrage 1995); 10 dots read faster than 100.

Goal progress

How close is Goa?

SavingsglancedefaultHome-eligible

Why: M6 saved/to-go (Kivetz 2006 goal gradient). Bangles stay as the complete motion, not the static form.

Goal ETA

When will I get there?

Savingsexploredefault

Why: Future-self path (M13: Hershfield 2011); time → glow allowed.

Savings growth

Am I saving more?

Savingsexploredefault

Why: Peak-end: end on progress (rec #71). Lanes are counted dots, comparable on a baseline.

Leftover rolled to savings

Where did last month's leftover go?

Savingsexploredefault

Why: Colour change from category to green is the whole story (green = savings only, P2e-Q2).

Owed to you

Who owes me?

Spendingexploredefault

Why: Outside the budget, dashed (v7/v11 language).

Month story

How did the month end?

Insightsexploredefault

Why: Peak-end + fresh start (Dai et al. via v11); frames end on what you kept.

Equivalents

What does this mean in my terms?

Insightsexploredefault

Why: Own frequent buys as the unit (M5: Barrio 2016; Riederer 2018; decided P2c-Q3). Used as the perspective line across cards.

Money as time (days of a jar)

How many days is this?

Insightsdetaillibrary

Why: M10 days-of-jar avoids hours-of-work for non-earners (Whillans 2017). Still open (P2c-Q5): library only.

Month by month

Long view?

Insightsdetaillibrary

Why: Counted lanes on one baseline; current month in colour, past as outline.

Where money sits

How much do I have, where?

Incomeexploredefault

Why: Balance split (rec #59) in the shared vocabulary: jars, held, saved, owed.

Phase 4 Structure

Where everything lives. Five tabs, Pay one tap from anywhere, three layers per tab (glance → explore → detail) plus settings one decision per screen. Phone mockups use the locked dot system with the same seed month; Home carries no numbers. Phone frames are drawn dark like the reference.

Tab map

Home: three layouts

Same widgets, three arrangements. Bell has a soft dot and no count. Avatar = app-wide settings.

Where Pay lives

Target: Scan in 1 tap from every tab; UPI ID and Log cash in no more than 2.

How deeper layers open

M1 Push screens

Every layer is a new screen. Clear back path, but you lose the board each time and it takes more taps.

M2 Expand in place

Cards grow in place. Keeps context, but detail views (lists, history) make the page very long.

M3 Hybrid · recommended

Explore opens in place (one card at a time). Detail and every settings step push a screen, so each screen holds one decision.

Other structure choices

ChoiceABCRec
Settings / drawerA: gear per tab + avatar on Home for app-wideB: one avatar drawerC: drawer + tab shortcutA
Bell placementA: Home header only; full screen, "Needs you" on top, activity below; soft dot, no countB: bell on every tab headerC: bottom sheet over HomeA
Bell behaviourA: Needs-you items leave when done; activity kept 90 days, filter by tabB: everything stays until swipedC: activity only, actions as pushA
Widget customisationA: Home pin/hide/reorder (max 6) · Insights pin from library · others fixed, can hideB: fixed everywhereC: all tabs customisableA
Intro pageA: one page, one visual, 3 lines, Got it; ? in headerB: 3-step carouselC: coach marks on real UIA

Tab intros

Shown on first visit, reopened from "?". One visual, three lines, one button.

Bell

Questions for Tarun

P4-Q1

Home layout

  • A: Widget grid like the reference: wide Pace glow on top, then half and wide cards, add-widget tile
  • B: Big glow hero + three stacked cards
  • C: Single-column story (sentence + small visual)

Recommend A. Grid is the most scannable and the user owns the order. Every card is a doorway to a tab, so Home stays at about 6 marks per card and no numbers (Kay 2016: few countable marks; Weiser & Brown: calm periphery). C reads well once but gets long and is harder to customise.

P4-Q2

Where Pay lives

  • A: Round Pay button beside the floating tab pill. Tap = camera open (Scan); "Pay UPI ID" and "Log cash" sit under the viewfinder
  • B: Centre button inside the tab bar (6 slots)
  • C: Persistent three-part pill above the tab bar
  • D: Big Pay button on Home only

Recommend A. A keeps Scan at 1 tap from every tab and the other two at 2 taps on one screen. B makes an odd 2 | Pay | 3 bar. C costs a row of screen on every tab. D is 2 taps from any other tab.

P4-Q3

How deeper layers open

  • A: Hybrid — a card opens in place to explore (one open at a time), detail and settings push a new screen
  • B: Every layer is a new screen
  • C: Everything expands in place

Recommend A. Opening in place keeps the context (Sweller 1988: less to hold in mind); pushing for detail and settings keeps "one decision per screen" and a clear back path. C gets long and loses the back button.

P4-Q4

Where settings live

  • A: Gear in each tab header for that tab, avatar on Home for app-wide settings
  • B: One avatar drawer for everything
  • C: Drawer, with a shortcut from each tab

Recommend A. Matches the locked rule that editing lives in each tab. App-wide items (look, UPI IDs, notifications, lock) have no tab, so they go behind the avatar.

P4-Q5

Customising widgets

  • A: Home: pin, hide, reorder (max 6). Insights: pin from the library. Other tabs: fixed order, can hide
  • B: Fixed everywhere
  • C: Every tab fully customisable

Recommend A. Home and Insights are where taste differs. Fixed order in Income, Spending and Savings keeps the money story in one order (in → spend → keep) and makes the intros stay true.

Notes: claude/v12_phase4_structure.md

Phase 5 Core flows

14 flows as storyboards on the decided structure (widget Home, Pay beside the tab bar, hybrid depth, gear per tab). The 6 key flows have 2–3 variants each. Money model: Money in → Savings + Spending money; Spending money = Subscriptions (come out on their own) + jars. One decision per screen, no red, no debt words. Tap counts start from wherever the student is.

Recommended path per flow

#FlowVariantsRecommendedTapsDecisions
1First run + budget setup3B Starter month43
2Budget edit1Gear → jar → amount31
3Income arrival + split3A Ask once, split21
4Pay: scan → amount → jar → UPI3A Jar as a chip on the amount screen21
5Empty jar3A Ask once at pay21
6Log cash / manual entry1Pay → Log cash chip31
7Sort an unknown UPI payment1Bell → 3 chips21
8Subscriptions1Add · auto-deduct · price · cancel31
9Split with friends + owed back3A Toggle at pay32
10Refund1Match to the original spend21
11Savings goal1Create · add · reached · withdraw21
12Month-end3A Choice, then story21
13Move money between jars1From the jar31
14Bell actions1Needs-you on top21

Storyboards

Flow 1First run + budget setup Global

Recommend: B. 4 taps, 3 decisions. The student-type pick does the work the 7 screens of A did; each layer is still editable one tap away (one decision per screen). Manual path: same 4 screens with "What comes in each month?" in place of the link.

A One question per screen

7 taps · 7 decisions

Every money layer gets its own screen and the dots build up as you go. Clear, but 7 screens before the app.

B Starter month

recommended4 taps · 3 decisions

Student type picks a full starter month (savings, subscriptions found on AutoPay, jars). One "Looks right" accepts it; "Change one thing" opens only that layer. Manual path skips the link step and asks "What comes in?" instead.

C Learn first

3 taps · 2 decisions

Fewest taps, but needs 30 days of UPI history; does not work for manual-only users or new accounts.

Flow 2Budget edit Spending

Recommend: One version. 3 taps. Each screen changes one thing; the total never changes unless you edit Money in.

Gear → jar → amount

recommended3 taps · 1 decision

Total stays the same: dots come from the jar you pick (default: the one with most left).

Flow 3Income arrival + split Income

Recommend: A for regular sources (2 taps, 1 decision), C for irregular ones (3 taps). B becomes the "Split on its own" setting after 3 months of same-split confirms.

A Ask once, split

recommended2 taps · 1 decision

Regular income: one sheet, one button, undo toast. Grey dots turn into jar colours as they settle.

B Silent auto-split

0 taps · 0 decisions

Zero taps, but money moving without the student seeing it is the thing v7 testing called confusing. Good as an opt-in setting later.

C Irregular income

recommended3 taps · 2 decisions

For gig/one-off money: first ask what it is for (also catches friends paying back), then show the split. Used when the source is not a known regular one.

Flow 4Pay: scan → amount → jar → UPI Pay

Recommend: A. 2 taps to UPI hand-off from any tab, 1 decision (amount). Jar chip remembers the payee; per-day figure appears only when the jar is low.

A Jar as a chip on the amount screen

recommended2 taps · 1 decision

Pay → camera reads QR (0 taps) → amount with the guessed jar already picked and the repeat line → Pay. Dots drop through the hourglass while UPI opens.

B Jar first

3 taps · 2 decisions

Seeing the jar before the amount is calming, but adds a decision every time even when the guess is right (it is for ~8 in 10 payees).

C Pause screen

3 taps · 2 decisions

A moment of friction with the per-day figure (research: a pause helps), but the extra screen on every chai gets skipped fast.

Flow 5Empty jar Pay

Recommend: A + C. 2 taps. Never red, never "over". Food's future lanes shrink a little across all days rather than one blank day.

A Ask once at pay

recommended2 taps · 1 decision

Before UPI opens: one sentence, one button using the jar with most left. Remaining days re-spread (P2e-Q5).

B Pay first, sort after

1 taps · 1 decision

Never blocks the queue at the counter, but the student finds out after the fact.

C All jars empty

recommended2 taps · 1 decision

Only when nothing is left anywhere: next month lighter is the default, savings is the second chip. No debt words.

Flow 6Log cash / manual entry Pay

Recommend: One version. 3 taps.

Pay → Log cash chip

recommended3 taps · 1 decision

Same amount screen as Pay, so there is one thing to learn. Import sits in Spending settings as a placeholder.

Flow 7Sort an unknown UPI payment Bell

Recommend: One version. 2 taps.

Bell → 3 chips

recommended2 taps · 1 decision

Tapping a guess sorts it; "remember" is on by default.

Flow 8Subscriptions Income

Recommend: One version. Add 3 taps; deduct 0; price change 1; cancel reminder 1.

Add · auto-deduct · price · cancel

recommended3 taps · 1 decision

Add in 3 taps (AutoPay prefill); due day needs 0 taps; reminder the day before has Keep / I'll cancel.

Flow 9Split with friends + owed back Pay / Spending

Recommend: A at pay (3 taps) and B from the spend (4 taps) share one screen. Remind = share sheet with UPI link; paying back returns dots to the jar.

A Toggle at pay

recommended3 taps · 2 decisions

Split switch on the amount screen, then friends. Owed money shows as dashed dots in the jar until it comes back.

B From spend detail

recommended4 taps · 2 decisions

For bills split after the meal. Same "who" screen.

C Split later via bell

3 taps · 2 decisions

Pending reminder; useful, but one more item in the bell.

Flow 10Refund Bell

Recommend: One version. 2 taps.

Match to the original spend

recommended2 taps · 1 decision

Refund chip is preselected when an earlier payment to the same payee matches.

Flow 11Savings goal Savings

Recommend: One version. Create 2, add 1, withdraw 2 taps.

Create · add · reached · withdraw

recommended2 taps · 1 decision

Quick-add chips; reaching it plays the bangle close (one "!"); withdrawing shows the new ETA, no PIN, no guilt.

Flow 12Month-end Bell / Insights

Recommend: A. 1 tap to save leftover, 1 to open the story. Default button is Savings; leftover kept rolls into next month's jars.

A Choice, then story

recommended2 taps · 1 decision

One decision on the notification; the month story waits in Insights as a pinned card.

B Auto-sweep

0 taps · 0 decisions

Fastest, but the student never sees the win.

C Story first

3 taps · 1 decision

Nice ritual, but three screens before the one action; drop-off risk.

Flow 13Move money between jars Spending

Recommend: One version. 3 taps.

From the jar

recommended3 taps · 1 decision

Dots slide across; total stays the same.

Flow 14Bell actions Home

Recommend: One version. 2 taps per item.

Needs-you on top

recommended2 taps · 1 decision

Each needs-you row acts in place: Sort, Decide, Remind, Split. Done rows drop into activity.

Questions for Tarun

P5-Q1

Onboarding

  • A: one question per screen (7)
  • B: starter month from student type (4)
  • C: learn from 30 days of UPI (3)

Recommend B. Fewest decisions that still works for manual-only users; every layer is one tap from its tab settings later.

P5-Q2

Income split

  • A: ask once + undo for regular, one question for irregular
  • B: silent auto-split
  • C: always ask what it is for

Recommend A. One confirm keeps the student aware of the split; auto-split can be offered after 3 same confirms.

P5-Q3

Jar at pay

  • A: guessed jar as a chip on the amount screen (2 taps)
  • B: jar first (3)
  • C: a pause screen with per-day figure (3)

Recommend A. Guess is right most of the time; per-day line appears only when the jar is low (P2c-Q1).

P5-Q4

Empty jar timing

  • A: ask once before UPI opens
  • B: pay first, sort after

Recommend A. Student decides with the facts in front of them; one button; days re-spread after.

P5-Q5

Month-end leftover

  • A: one choice, then story in Insights
  • B: auto-sweep to Savings
  • C: story first, choice last

Recommend A. The win is seen and chosen; story stays available without blocking.

Phase 6 Visual identity

Four complete style directions, each shown on the same four screens with the same data (Tarun, hostel, ₹9,000 month: Food ₹4,000, Travel ₹1,500, Fun ₹1,500, Savings ₹2,000). Static only; motion and sound come in Phase 12.

Locked going in

  • Dot ladder: crumb (pie wedge) <₹100 → dot ₹100 → pill ₹1,000 → block ₹10,000. Left = solid jar colour, spent = outline.
  • Three colour-safe jar hues (amber, blue, plum), patterns for jar 4+; savings green only; income in neutral ink; no red.
  • Glow only for time and position (pace, today, next money in, goal ETA). Colour default, B&W option.
  • Widget-grid Home with no numbers; round Pay button beside the floating tab bar.

The four directions

Each tile: palette tokens, type pairing, card and dot anatomy, then Home, Spending (day lanes), Savings goal and Pay amount. Second row: the B&W option.

A

Monochrome glow

Faithful to the reference: near-black, soft widget cards, white glow for time only. Colour lives only in the dots.

Logo options

Each mark in light and dark. All use only the dot vocabulary.

L1 · Dot + crumb

One ₹100 dot with a pie-wedge crumb dripping below. Continues the v11 tile-and-drip mark in the v12 dot language.

L2 · Dot jar

A jar outline holding 3×3 dots; the top row is outlined (spent), the rest solid. Reads as "budget jar" at a glance.

L3 · Trickle

Three dots falling and shrinking left to right, the last one a crumb. The name drawn as motion.

L4 · Pill + dot (t)

A ₹1,000 pill crossed by a column of dots forms a lowercase t. Ties the logo to the money ladder.

Splash (static), L1 in each direction

trickle
Monochrome glow
trickle
Warm paper
trickle
Ink & dots
trickle
Soft night

Recommendation: A · Monochrome glow

It is the reference Tarun picked for Home, and it keeps the one rule that makes Trickle readable: colour appears only on money. The near-black ground gives the white glow a job (time and position) without it ever touching a dot.

  • Borrow from C: 1.6px outlines for spent dots, so spent reads clearly at 4px radius.
  • Borrow from B: its validated palette as the light companion (amber #b7791f, blue #2f63c9, plum #93306b, savings #1f9b84).
  • Keep Geist for display and text, with tabular figures for ₹.
  • Logo L1, dot + crumb.

Watch

  • Fun ↔ Savings is the weakest pair for deutan vision (ΔE 7.6): never show them side by side without names.
  • On dark, outlined spent dots at 1.3px can vanish on small widgets. Use 1.6px.
  • D is the calmest, but its muted hues fail the separation target at the size Home uses.

Questions for Tarun

P6-Q1

Which style direction?

  • A: Monochrome glow
  • B: Warm paper
  • C: Ink & dots
  • D: Soft night

Recommended: A, borrowing C’s 1.6px spent outlines and B’s palette as the light companion.

P6-Q2

Default appearance?

  • A: Dark by default, light in Settings
  • B: Follow the phone
  • C: Light by default

Recommended: B: follow the phone. Both modes are validated; the reference look shows whenever the phone is dark.

P6-Q3

Logo mark?

  • L1: Dot + crumb
  • L2: Dot jar
  • L3: Trickle
  • L4: Pill + dot (t)

Recommended: L1: smallest shape that still says "money in dots", works at 16px, and carries over from v11.

P6-Q4

Numerals for ₹ amounts?

  • A: Mono, tabular (Geist Mono)
  • B: Same face as text, tabular figures
  • C: Display face

Recommended: B: tabular Geist keeps amounts calm; mono reads technical on the Pay screen.

P6-Q5

Dot finish?

  • A: Flat + hairline highlight
  • B: Embossed press
  • C: Perfectly flat

Recommended: A: a 1px highlight separates touching dots on dark cards without looking like a glow.

Phase 7 Retention & emotional design

How Trickle brings a student back without guilt, games or noise. All mockups in direction A (Monochrome glow, Geist), same hostel-student data as Phase 6. Values held: savings motivates; friction at pay; repeat-buy awareness; low anxiety; no red, no debt words, no badges or counts; no streaks; Home shows no numbers; the bell holds actions and the log.

Logged from Phase 6 (Tarun, 1 Oct)

  • Direction A Monochrome glow (Geist / Geist Mono) + C's 1.6px spent outlines + B's palette for light mode.
  • Appearance follows the phone; B&W optional. Logo: L3 "Trickle" wordmark. Dots: flat + hairline highlight. ₹ numerals: text face, tabular figures.

First week, day 0 to 7

Filled glow = reward moment, ring = the one push of the week, dashed = deliberate silence. Return triggers: day 2 (first-day recap), day 7 (first check-in), day 30 (month story).

  1. Day 0
    Setup

    Starter month (4 taps). Savings dots already dropped in: progress starts at more than zero.

  2. Day 1

Lock-screen mockups, same week. Wording never carries a remaining-budget number.

Max 1 a day, 3 a week, nothing 22:00–08:00. Only five types: income split, subscription tomorrow, weekly check-in, month story, one welcome-back. Each one has one action.

  • Pace 4×1Glow of the month, today lit, one word. No numbers. Updates after each pay.
  • Goal 2×2Saved solid, to-go outlined. Tap opens Savings.
  • Pay 2×1One tap to scan: puts the pay moment (friction) before the UPI app.
  • Jar 2×2Optional. The one widget with a budget look; off by default, user adds it.

Sharing and personalisation

  • Share card (opt-in)From the last month-story card: dots and the month name only. "Show amounts" is off by default. No friend list, no leaderboard.
  • Your own unitsEquivalents use the student's frequent buys ("≈ 3 of your chais").
  • Your own rhythmCheck-in day and time, quiet hours and each notification type are editable in app settings; weekly or payday period follows Income settings.
  • Widget choicePace, Goal and Pay by default; Jar widget opt-in.

14 principles

  1. 1. Savings shows up firstEvery loop that ends, ends on savings: income split, check-in, month story.Thaler & Benartzi 2004; Kahneman et al. 1993 (peak-end)
  2. 2. One tap per loop, two loops need noneRetention comes from removing effort, not adding prompts.Fogg 2009 B=MAP
  3. 3. Bad news only where it can be acted onJar empty appears at the pay moment, never on open or as a push.Karlsson, Loewenstein & Seppi 2009 (ostrich effect)
  4. 4. Fresh starts are built inSunday and the 1st reset the frame; returning after a gap is a fresh start too.Dai, Milkman & Riis 2014
  5. 5. Progress starts above zeroSetup drops savings dots in before the first spend.Nunes & Drèze 2006 (endowed progress)
  6. 6. No streaks, scores or badgesMissed days are invisible, so there is nothing to break.Polivy & Herman 1985 (what-the-hell effect); v8 research §14
  7. 7. Few, predictable notifications≤1/day, ≤3/week, quiet 22:00–08:00, a channel per type the user can mute.Android notification guidelines; Pielot et al. 2014; Wohllebe et al. 2021
  8. 8. Every notification has one useful actionIf it has no action and no news, it is not sent.Android notification guidelines
  9. 9. Feel the paymentDots leave at pay; the widget puts Pay before the UPI app.Prelec & Loewenstein 1998; Soman 2003
  10. 10. Name the habit, never judge itRepeat buys as counts in the user's own units ("3rd chai"), no adjectives.Soman 2001; P2c-Q3
  11. 11. Explain the unexpected calmlyLate income, withdrawals and empty jars each get a sentence that says what happens next.Shapiro & Burchell 2012 (financial anxiety)
  12. 12. Calm celebrationOne motion, one soft tone, once. No confetti.Weiser & Brown 1996 (calm technology)
  13. 13. Sharing is opt-in and shows dots, not ₹Month story card can be shared; amounts hidden unless switched on.Wrapped-style recap sharing; privacy line (Phase 1 #133)
  14. 14. Ambient beats alertingThe widget and Home glow carry the daily loop instead of pushes.Weiser & Brown 1996; Ambient Orb (v8 research §12)

Sources (new this phase): Android Developers — Notifications design guidelines · Wohllebe et al. 2021 — Effect of push notification frequency on app user behaviour (retail) · Pielot, Church & de Oliveira 2014 — An in-situ study of mobile phone notifications (MobileHCI) · Dai, Milkman & Riis 2014 — The fresh start effect (Management Science) · Lee — Fintech nudges: overspending messages (SSRN) · Bitrián, Buil & Catalán 2021 — Gamification of personal finance apps · Spotify Wrapped as a shareable recap (NoGood case study). Others carried from v8 research and v11 Phase 7.

Recommendation

  • Notifications A: ≤1/day, ≤3/week, quiet 22:00–08:00, five types, one action each.
  • Check-in A: one card ending "Start the new week".
  • Month story A: five cards ending on "You kept ₹X"; B's poster as the opt-in share card.
  • Return A: "Welcome back", savings first, start from today.
  • Widgets: Pace 4×1, Goal 2×2, Pay 2×1; Jar opt-in.

Watch

  • Fewer pushes means the widget has to earn its place; test whether students add it.
  • "₹2,640" on the story card is the one big number; it stays in Insights, never on Home.
  • Late income copy must never guess why.
